texts: good. the report is one past event with Hesper as the one reporting and the Council as addressee, the date sits on the report, and the cost claim is held inside it rather than asserted as fact — which is what a report should give you — with "about" kept as a spread around 1.5 rather than dropped. The measure phrase "vessels of mire-essence" has no licensed unit form, so the translator coins one; that was reviewed and accepted, and no rewrite of the phrase avoids it.

good. the held-supply claim is sealed under Hesper's report with the store as the holder, the winter supply kept inside the report where it belongs, and the compound kinds unpacked to their genus. "Eight weeks of winter supply" again lands on an improvised measure (a duration attached to a stock rather than to an event), which was reviewed and accepted as the best available form.

good. the production is typed and Northcove is named at top level, while "was normal" and the Northcove link both stay inside the report — so the parse records that Brindle Coombe said it, not that the production actually was normal.

good. the report holds a twelve-days-ahead ordering for that new moon, and the compound is unpacked to moon and new. "Next" itself gets no atom of its own (there is no licensed form for an ordering modifier on an entity), but the twelve-day ordering already places it as the upcoming one, so the reading is not widened.

bad: the reported group size is flattened to a bare count on the party — the "having" is gone, the count hangs on a symbol with no group of members behind it, and the word "members" is never recorded, so "who is in the party?" or "how many members?" has nothing to bind to. Rewrite as "Sailsworn reported to the Council that twelve members would form the salt-bloom harvest party." — a plain counted plural in the clause gets both the twelve-member group and its size recorded, and naming the party here exactly as the next sentence names it keeps it one kind instead of two unrelated ones.

good. the proposal is reified with Old Vesh as the one proposing and the joining held inside it, so nothing asserts that Coraline Ash actually joined; both names are recorded at top level and the party's kind and genus come out. (The party currently carries two unlinked kind symbols across this sentence and the previous one; the rewrite suggested there settles it.)

mixed: the sentence itself parses faithfully — a past agree event with the Council as agent — but nothing records what was agreed to, so the outcome of the whole passage, the proposal being accepted, never reaches the knowledge base. Rewrite as "The Council agreed that Coraline Ash would join the salt-bloom harvest party." so the agreed content is carried inside the agreement and reuses the same person and party already introduced.
